hypotheses.statement: The concurrency increase from 8 to 32 workers caused database connection pool exhaustion because the pool size (20) was insufficient for the increased worker count.
The expired service token caused failures when workers could not read the settlement_v2_enabled flag, as the system fails closed when unable to read feature flags.
The two faults (pool exhaustion and token expiry) were independent and coincidental, starting four minutes apart, with neither explaining the other.
The combined failure rate of approximately 0.61 resulted from overlapping pool_timeout errors (0.38) and token-related failures (0.31), with some attempts experiencing both.

observed_facts.statement: Configuration change at 15:55:00Z raised settlement-worker concurrency from 8 to 32 workers while database connection pool size remained at 20.
Database connection pool exhausted from 15:58:10Z with pool size 20, checked-out 20, causing pool_timeout errors after 5000ms affecting approximately 0.38 of attempts.
Service token for flags.internal expired at 15:59:00Z on 2026-02-11 after 90 days, issued on 2025-11-13, with renewal not automated.
Calls to flags.internal returning 401 invalid_token from 15:59:02Z, affecting approximately 0.31 of attempts, overlapping with pool_timeout failures.
Settlement failure ratio reached 0.61 against objective of 0.02 at 16:00:44Z, alert fired and did not clear until 18:12:30Z.
Connection pool raised to 64 at 17:20:15Z, pool_timeout errors stopped, failure ratio fell from 0.61 to 0.29.
Replacement token for flags.internal installed at 18:12:10Z, 401 responses stopped, failure ratio fell from 0.29 to 0.004.
Failure ratio series shows two distinct step changes: 0.61 to 0.29 at 17:20Z and 0.29 to 0.004 at 18:12Z, each aligned with a different remediation.

open_questions.missing_evidence: Design documentation or configuration management rationale explaining the relationship between worker count and pool size
open_questions.question: Why is the database connection pool size not derived from or automatically adjusted based on worker concurrency?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Inventory of service tokens with their issuance dates, expiry dates, and renewal automation status
open_questions.question: Which other service tokens are on manual renewal schedules and may be at risk of similar expiry?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Financial impact assessment or settlement value metrics during the failure window
open_questions.question: What was the settlement value at risk during the incident period?

summary: Payment settlement failures occurred due to two independent, coincidental faults: (1) database connection pool exhaustion after worker concurrency increased without corresponding pool size adjustment, and (2) expired service token preventing feature flag reads. The combined failure rate reached 61%, resolved in two steps: pool enlargement reduced failures to 29%, and token replacement resolved remaining failures to 0.4%.

timeline.statement: pool enlarged, failures reduced but not resolved
responder expects full recovery after pool fix
